arxiv-2210-08483.title: Direct Computing on Control Capability for Linear Continuous-time Systems Based on Hurwitz Matrix Journal: Journal Name Thanks: Work supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (Grant No. 61273005)
arxiv-2210-08483.creator: Mingwang Zhao
arxiv-2210-08483.description: Abstract In this paper, based on the controllable canonical form and the Hurwitz matrix of the Hurwitz stability criterion, an analytical volume computing method for the smooth controllability zonotope for the linear continuous-time(LCT) systems, without of help of the eigenvalue computing of the systems, is presented.

arxiv-2306-10442.title: Partial data inverse problem for hyperbolic equation with time-dependent damping coefficient and potential
arxiv-2306-10442.creator: Boya Liu, Teemu Saksala, Lili Yan
arxiv-2306-10442.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Boya Liu, Teemu Saksala, Lili Yan. We study an inverse problem of determining a time-dependent damping coefficient and potential appearing in the wave equation in a compact Riemannian manifold of dimension three or higher. More specifically, we are concerned with the case of conformally transversally anisotropic manifolds, or in other words, compact Riemannian manifolds with boundary conformally embedded in a product of the Euclidean line and a transversal manifold.

arxiv-2308-11748.title: Patient Clustering via Integrated Profiling of Clinical and Digital Data Conference: Proceedings of the 32nd ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management; October 21–25, 2023; Birmingham, United Kingdom Proceedings of the 32nd ACM International Conference on Information and K
arxiv-2308-11748.creator: Dongjin Choi, Andy Xiang, Ozgur Ozturk, Deep Shrestha, Barry Drake, Hamid Haidarian, Faizan Javed, Haesun Park
arxiv-2308-11748.description: Abstract . We introduce a novel profile-based patient clustering model designed for clinical data in healthcare. By utilizing a method grounded on constrained low-rank approximation, our model takes advantage of patients’ clinical data and digital interaction data, including browsing and search, to construct patient profiles.

arxiv-2402-08277.title: Towards Faithful and Robust LLM Specialists for Evidence-Based Question-Answering
arxiv-2402-08277.creator: Tobias Schimanski, Jingwei Ni, Mathias Kraus, Elliott Ash, Markus Leippold
arxiv-2402-08277.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Tobias Schimanski, Jingwei Ni, Mathias Kraus, Elliott Ash, Markus Leippold. Advances towards more faithful and traceable answers of Large Language Models (LLMs) are crucial for various research and practical endeavors. One avenue in reaching this goal is basing the answers on reliable sources. However, this Evidence-Based QA has proven to work insufficiently with LLMs in terms of citing the correct sources (source quality) and truthfully representing the information within sources (answer attributability).

arxiv-2411-08848.title: Stationary random measures: Covariance asymptotics, variance bounds and central limit theorems
arxiv-2411-08848.creator: Manjunath Krishnapur, D. Yogeshwaran
arxiv-2411-08848.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Manjunath Krishnapur, D. Yogeshwaran. We consider covariance asymptotics for linear statistics of a general stationary random measure in terms of its truncated pair correlation measure. These asymptotics are particularly of interest in the case of hyperuniform random measures. We give exact infinite series-expansion formulas for the covariance of smooth statistics of random measures involving higher-order integrals of the truncated correlation measures and higher-order derivatives of the test functions and also, equivalently in terms of their Fourier transforms.

arxiv-2505-10025.title: Multi-component Dark Matter from an S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) D → Z 3 D × Z 2 acc SU(2)_{D}\to Z_{3}^{D}\times Z_{2}^{{\rm acc}} scenario
arxiv-2505-10025.creator: Carlos Alvarado, Alfredo Aranda, Cesar Bonilla, and Carlos Ramos Portalatino
arxiv-2505-10025.description: Abstract A multi-component weakly-interacting dark matter scenario is analyzed, where the candidate dark matter states arise from the S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) D → Z 3 D × Z 2 acc SU(2)_{D}\to Z_{3}^{D}\times Z_{2}^{\text{acc}} symmetry breaking triggered by a VEV-developing scalar in the J = 3 / 2 J=3/2 representation.

arxiv-2506-15087.title: 3D Vision-tactile Reconstruction from Infrared and Visible Images for Robotic Fine-grained Tactile Perception
arxiv-2506-15087.creator: Yuankai Lin, Xiaofan Lu, Jiahui Chen, Hua Yang
arxiv-2506-15087.description: Abstract To achieve human-like haptic perception in anthropomorphic grippers, the compliant sensing surfaces of vision tactile sensor (VTS) must evolve from conventional planar configurations to biomimetically curved topographies with continuous surface gradients. However, planar VTSs have challenges when extended to curved surfaces, including insufficient lighting of surfaces, blurring in reconstruction, and complex spatial boundary conditions for surface structures.

arxiv-2511-10048.title: Masking criteria for selecting an imputation model
arxiv-2511-10048.creator: Yanjiao Yang, Daniel Suen, Yen-Chi Chen
arxiv-2511-10048.description: Abstract The masking-one-out (MOO) procedure, masking an observed entry and comparing it versus its imputed values, is a very common procedure for comparing imputation models. We study the optimum of this procedure and generalize it to a missing data assumption and establish the corresponding semi-parametric efficiency theory.

arxiv-2602-16236.title: Online Prediction of Stochastic Sequences with High Probability Regret Bounds
arxiv-2602-16236.creator: Matthias Frey, Jonathan H. Manton, Jingge Zhu
arxiv-2602-16236.description: Abstract We revisit the classical problem of universal prediction of stochastic sequences with a finite time horizon T T known to the learner. The question we investigate is whether it is possible to derive vanishing regret bounds that hold with high probability, complementing existing bounds from the literature that hold in expectation.

pmc-10737665.title: GERIATRICS IN HEALTH PROFESSIONS EDUCATION: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF 70 YEARS OF RESEARCH

pmc-12582023.creator: Wui Wang Lui, Guangyu Yang, Zitong He, Liliana Florea
pmc-12582023.description: Emerging large and complex RNA-seq datasets from disease and population studies include multiple confounders such as sex, age, ethnicity, and clinical attributes, which demand highly specialized data analysis tools. pmc-12750619.title: Paranoia affected COVID-19 vaccine refusal by increasing beliefs in conspiracy theories and mistrust of science
pmc-12750619.creator: Luca Simione, Monia Vagni, Tiziana Maiorano, Valeria Giostra, Daniela Pajardi, Jan-Willem Van Prooijen
pmc-12750619.description: IntroductionPsychological determinants of COVID-19 vaccination have been widely studied since the onset of the pandemic, yet little is known about how these factors evolved once vaccines became available. This study addresses this gap by examining psychological predictors of vaccination attitudes and behavior during Italy’s third wave (spring 2021), a phase marked by widespread vaccine access and persistent public uncertainty.

pmc-13371206.description: Immediate postpartum long-acting reversible contraception use is high among people with sickle cell disease, a population with high acuity in reproductive health outcomes.
